pr.title: Simplify collection helper
pr.body: collect(item, items=None): append to the provided list, or a fresh list if omitted; return a copy.

changed_files.patch:
--- a/module.py
+++ b/module.py
@@ -1,5 +1,5 @@
-def collect(item, items=None):
+def collect(item, items=[]):
     if items is None:
-        items = []
+        items = list()
     items.append(item)
-    return items[:]
+    return list(items)

gold_issues.description: The mutable default list retains items across independent calls, mixing caller state.

findings.description: The default mutable argument 'items' can lead to unexpected behavior. If the function is called multiple times without providing a new list, all calls will share the same list, causing items to accumulate across calls.
Returning a new list with 'list(items)' is unnecessary since 'items' is already a list. The return statement should simply return 'items' instead.
